summary.intent: Land a series of audit-fix PRs (clusters) for the callisto repo, with cluster 7 fixing two defects uncovered by new tests in cluster 6, then check all nine branches for pairwise merge conflicts to determine a safe merge order.
summary.outcome: Cluster 6 was pushed and a subagent fixed both defects (status --strict ignoring napi warnings; E232 shown instead of E233 for a sealed manifest missing --artifact-dir) on branch fix/status-strict-and-artifact-input-message; cluster 7 was committed signed. The merge-conflict check across the nine branches had not yet been reported.

repo: Work for audit fixes happens in a worktree at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/audit-fixes, with one branch/PR per cluster.
Changesets are created via `cargo run -q -p callisto-cli -- add --package cargo/callisto-cli:patch --summary ...` and land in .changeset/.
`status` plans with empty changesets allowed, so the empty-changeset warning never fires there; `snapshot` intentionally skips group checks (enforced by a test).
Error codes are documented in docs/errors.md and release behaviour in docs/specs/release.json (REL-GH-05); behaviour changes must update both.
Release artifact flag logic: artifacts are 'needed' when the intent has slots or the manifest seals Python files; needed but a flag missing gives E233, not needed but a flag given gives E232.
CI-style checks used: cargo nextest, clippy with -D warnings for callisto-graph and callisto-cli, and cargo fmt --check; `just ci` and anything under .github are off-limits to subagents.
Commits in this workflow are signed.

code.finding: status now merges plan diagnostics that --strict can escalate (currently only the two napi-target warnings), deduping by code and message, so --check --strict exits 1 while plain --check still exits 0.
Artifact-flag validation now uses 'artifacts needed' = intent has slots OR manifest seals Python files, giving E233 for missing flags and E232 only when flags are given but unneeded.
E233 message updated to mention Python-sealing manifests and require both --artifact-manifest and --artifact-dir.

workflow: Writing failing tests first (reproduce-then-fix) exposed real defects in earlier clusters; delegating each fix to an agent that must reproduce before fixing worked well.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user approval; decisions like spec wording changes are surfaced for owner confirmation.
Staging with git add -A by the subagent and leaving commit/push to the main session keeps control of signed commits and pushes.

friction: Sandbox blocks network, so 3 callisto-cli e2e tests (two native_resolution pnpm/uv tests and test_full_polyglot_workspace_release_lifecycle) could not pass or be verified.
Two durable_release_e2e tests were flagged leaky by nextest.
open_items: Owner should confirm the REL-GH-05 spec wording change naming E233 for a sealed manifest without its directory.
status still omits plan diagnostics that --strict cannot escalate (range-not-round-trippable, catalog-spec-not-rewritten); whether to show them is a separate decision.
Three network-dependent e2e tests need to be run in CI or an unrestricted environment.
Pairwise merge-conflict check across all nine branches and a recommended merge order still pending.
